main_text.l: sione[?] altissimi nihil potestatis habent. Tempestates autē, pruinas, grandines facere posse, id constanter pernegamus: sacrae literae nobis assentiuntur, quae tempestatis gubernatione soli & uni Deo tribuunt. Inquies, At fatentur, non tantū tormentis adactæ, sed & sponte & constanter quidem se turbasse aerem & tempestatem concitasse. Fateor quidem, sed meram (ut alia quoq; multa) Sathanicā esse impostu-ram vere ac liberè dico. Satan enim non tantū naturali ratione, & pro celeritate ingenij causas, loca & effectā tempestatū nouit, verum etiam iusta, irati Dei iudicia, volens nolensq; exequitur. Est enim ut ille ait, Dei carnifex. His rebus cognitis, hac pote-state cum mandatis accepta, illico complices accedit, stipulationis nefandæ admonet, ul-tionem iam diu optatam ipsis pollicetur, modum docet, nefandā sacrificia, quibus hæc cōficiuntur, monstrat. Invitas vi & verberibus cogit. Dirae & ultrices striges ultrò & coa-ctæ, tandem rem aggrediuntur. Voti compotes fiunt, lætantur, de tam tristi, abominan-dæ artis exitu. Iam quod voluit & plura e-tiam

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the first word, printed with a long-s-like initial, is read as "sione" and may be "Iove" or similar; marked [?]. "autē" and "quoq;" are read from small superscript marks and may be misread. "nouit" is read from "non uit" with the line break as printed. The word "tiam" at the foot is the catchword and is also the end of the last line, as printed. "nefandā" in the sentence "modum docet, nefanda sacrificia" is printed "nefanda", with the case as the printer set it; the accent-like mark over it is not clearly visible, so it is written as printed.
